Term1: Gram negative bacilli (other than pseudomonas) infections in bone or joint prostheses
Text:
# GRAM NEGATIVE BACILLI (OTHER THAN PSEUDOMONAS) INFECTIONS IN BONE OR JOINT

# PROSTHESES

For acute, moderate or severe infections, treat with intravenous antibiotics followed by oral antibiotics. Mild infections can be treated with oral antibiotics only.

Consult Infectious Diseases for specific management advice.

# Duration of Treatment

Treat for a total duration of 4-6 weeks. Chronic oral antimicrobial suppression may follow treatment based on individual patient circumstances.

References:

- Mandell chapter: Orthopedic Implant-Associated Infections
- Up-to-Date Article: Prosthetic Joint Infections: Treatment
- Osmon et al, Clinical Infectious Diseases (2013) 56.1, e1-25
- Sanford keyword: Prosthetic Joint Infection
Therapy:
## Oral Treatment For Mild Infections, Continuation of Therapy and Chronic

## Suppression

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID ($) R,DI

< OR >
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875-125 mg PO BID ($) R

## Alternative Oral Treatment for Intolerance to Above Oral Antibiotics

For treatment of mild infections and continuation of therapy
Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO BID ($) R,DI

For Chronic Suppression
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID ($) R,DI
